records.issue_text: Calendar updates use the current caller’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s credentials, so authorized attendees or team admins may update through—or fail against—the wrong calendar account.
records.rationale: The handler builds EventManager from the calling user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, while authorization explicitly permits non-organizer callers (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isAttendee`). So when an attendee or team admin calls addGuests, calendar attendee updates run against the caller's calendar credentials/destinationCalendar rather than the booking organizer's (`evt.destinationCalendar` comes from the booking organizer, but credentials are the caller's), which can fail or update the wrong calendar account. records.issue_text: Team members never receive the intended notification because the booking query does not load team members and the constructed `CalendarEvent` does not set `team`, leaving `calendarEvent.team?.members` absent.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.handler.ts builds the `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) without any `team` property, and the prisma query includes only attendees, eventType, destinationCalendar, references, and user — no team/members. Meanwhile sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts only sends OrganizerAddGuestsEmail to team members via `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)`, which will always be undefined here, so team member notifications are silently skipped.
